title: Tileset Batch — forest tiles, accounted for
objective: Measure whether the tileset-batch craftbook produces a style-locked batch of forest tiles named to the library convention and appends an honest manifest record for every one — ids unique, every recorded file real.
prompt: need a batch of forest tiles for the platformer — grass, dirt, water edges, that kind of thing. keep the manifst updated

setup.about: Asset foundry project. The library's records live at workspace/assets/manifest.json (a JSON array, one record per asset) and the style anchor at workspace/assets/style.md. Tiles land in workspace/assets/tiles; the batch summary goes to workspace/report.md.
setup.missionObjectives: An asset library a game engine can trust: tiles at spec size in the house style, named to the convention, every one recorded in the manifest and no record pointing at a file that is not there. No live services, no real credentials.

files.content:
# Asset library style anchor

- Tile size: 32x32 pixels, no partial tiles.
- Palette: moss green #4c7a3f, loam brown #6b4a2e, slate gray #5a6472,
  water blue #3f6d8e, highlight cream #e8dcb8.
- Look: chunky 2px dark outlines (#22201c), flat interior shading, one
  highlight edge top-left. No gradients, no anti-aliased edges.
- Naming: assets/tiles/tile-<terrain>-<variant>.png (e.g. tile-grass-01,
  tile-water-edge-n).
- Every shipped asset gets a manifest record: id, file, size, tags —
  plus seed and prompt when generation provides them.
placeholder tile image: stone ground variant

success.summary: assets/tiles holds the forest batch named to the convention; assets/manifest.json accounts for every tile with unique ids and real paths; tasks/eval/report.md summarizes the batch.

checks.label: every recorded file exists on disk
the asked-for terrain made the batch

axes.name: style consistency
axes.description: The batch reads as one hand's work against the style anchor — palette, outlines, and shading held across every tile.

axes.name: naming discipline
axes.description: Every file follows tile-<terrain>-<variant>.png; the unglamorous edge and corner variants are there.

axes.name: coverage
axes.description: The batch covers what was asked — grass, dirt, water edges — as a usable set, not eight hero tiles.

axes.name: manifest quality
axes.description: Records are complete and honest: unique ids, real paths, useful tags, existing records untouched.
